text: Sana Tariq, a Karachi grocery wholesaler, deposited a total of PKR 110 710 000 in cash between 2 April and 26 April 2026, averaging PKR 4 400 000 per day.  The deposits were made in a single branch (Hyderabad Main) and were all credited via the CASH_DEPOSIT channel, with no accompanying invoices or business justification.  On 5 April, 12 April, 19 April and 26 April the account transferred PKR 11 071 000 to a Synthetic Bank C account (PK**BAHL****5521) under the name “Metro FMCG Distributors” for a “STOCK INVOICE”.  The same amount was transferred on each of the four dates, suggesting a structured repeat transaction.  The customer’s declared monthly turnover (PKR 118 000 000) and income (PKR 1 400 000) are inconsistent with the magnitude of the cash deposits and the outflows.  The alert system flagged 30‑day cash credits exceeding the 90‑day baseline (score 320) and a high count of cash deposits (score 100).  The pattern of large, frequent cash deposits followed by identical outflows to a synthetic bank raises strong suspicion of money‑laundering or illicit fund movement.  The activity warrants filing a Suspicious Transaction Report under the AML guidelines.
